page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.metal-48xl is a bare-metal storage-optimized instance engineered for data-intensive processing. The server is built on the arm64 architecture utilizing AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors running at 2.7 GHz. It features 192 dedicated physical cores with a one-to-one thread-to-core mapping, eliminating hyperthreading contention and hypervisor overhead. The hardware is configured with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 system memory, providing 8.0 GB per physical core, and includes 120000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 300 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not feature discrete GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark measurements indicate performance characteristics oriented around scale-out parallelism and storage throughput. Multi-threaded evaluations demonstrate top-tier execution, including a stress-ng multi-core score of 287164.37, Geekbench multi-core score of 20677.0, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression rate of 1270.14 GB/sec. Memory subsystem bandwidth reaches 897.06 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 13947.51 GB/sec under cached workloads. Operational storage benchmarks record PassMark database metrics of 46115.93 and Redis operations at 378.59 million operations per second. Conversely, single-core processing scores place within average performance distributions, with a Geekbench single-core result of 1666.0, and small-model LLM generation speeds show limitations at 28.16 tokens per second.

The dense hardware configuration provides strong resource consolidation, packaging high core counts, large DDR5 memory, and 120 TB of direct-attached NVMe storage into a single host. A primary architectural tradeoff involves the reliance on arm64 instruction sets, which exclude x86-specific extensions like AVX-512 while requiring software ecosystems compiled for ARMv9. The instance profile is suited for large distributed databases, fast caching clusters, real-time analytics engines, and high-throughput static web workloads demanding maximum local storage capacity and parallel execution.
